lessons.title: So … that → Such … that
lessons.content: Sentences using 'so … that' can be transformed into 'such … that' sentences. 'So + adjective/adverb + that + result' becomes 'such + a/an + adjective + noun + that + result'. The key is to identify the noun that the adjective describes.

details.concept: so + adj → such + a/an + adj + noun
details.explanation: Move the adjective after 'a/an' and add the noun it describes.
details.example: This book is so good that I can't put it down. → This is such a good book that I can't put it down.
details.burmese: ဒီစာအုပ်က အရမ်းကောင်းလို့ ငါလက်က မချနိုင်ဘူး။

details.concept: so + adj → such + a/an + adj + noun
details.explanation: Identify the noun from context and place it after the adjective.
details.example: The wind is so strong that we cannot go outside. → It is such a strong wind that we cannot go outside.
details.burmese: လေပင်က အရမ်းလျှော့လို့ ငါတို့ အပြင်မသွားနိုင်ကြဘူး။

lessons.title: Such … that → So … that
lessons.content: Sentences using 'such … that' can be transformed into 'so … that' sentences. 'Such + a/an + adjective + noun + that + result' becomes 'so + adjective/adverb + that + result'. Move the noun before the structure and use it as the subject.

details.concept: such + a/an + adj + noun → so + adj
details.explanation: Move the noun to the subject position and use 'so + adjective' without the noun.
details.example: It is such a strong wind that we cannot go outside. → The wind is so strong that we cannot go outside.
details.burmese: ဒါက အလိုက်လျှော့ပင်ဖစ်လို့ ငါတို့ အပြင်မသွားနိုင်ကြဘူး။

details.concept: such + a/an + adj + noun → so + adj
details.explanation: For plural nouns, remove the article 'a/an'.
details.example: The T-shirts were so cheap that we bought quite a lot. → They were such cheap T-shirts that we bought quite a lot.
details.burmese: အင်းကျီတွေက အရမ်းစျေးပေါလို့ ငါတို့ အများကြီး ဝယ်လိုက်တယ်။
